items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 10.2.9 at source lines 805-821: assuming excluded middle, an injection between cardinalities yields a surjection given a point of the source, hence a merely existing surjection when the source is merely inhabited, and assuming the axiom of choice a surjection yields a merely existing injection. The author's proof (source lines 822-832) has three parts that use different hypotheses: the first builds the surjection by a case distinction on whether a fiber is inhabited, which is legitimate precisely because injectivity makes the fibers mere propositions and excluded middle decides them (lines 823-826); the second is an induction on truncation (line 829); and the third extracts an injective map from a surjection by the axiom of choice and observes that any section of a surjection is injective (lines 830-831). The statement records the three implications and never says that the case distinction in the first part is where contradiction-freedom of the fibers is consumed.
